lines.dialogue: You want this. You wouldn’t have brought me this far if you didn’t.
Get me home. I’ll do the rest.
Hi, this is David Linn from the New York Times. May I speak to Susan? Thank you.

Hi, Susan, it’s David again. I was just calling to see if -- No, I figured we’d do the interview by phone, seeing as they’re no longer in the city. But we’d really love a photo of Mr. and Mrs. Schwartz to go along with the article. We’ve got a stringer out of Albuquerque who we like a lot. When are they scheduled to return home? Think maybe we could -- So, they’re home tonight, then. Gotcha. Are they still at, uh... the address I have is Upper Canyon Road. Is that? -- Oh, Tesuque. Is that near the Opera House? I hear that’s very nice.

Okay, then. Lemme call my photographer, check out his availability. No, no, their call. Any day this week, we’re at their disposal. I know the Schwartzes are very busy people. Listen, thank you so much for your time. You too. Bye-bye.
Hey, Gretchen. Elliott.
I like your new house.
Are we looking east? God, you must have one great view of the Sangre de Cristos.
I saw you on Charlie Rose. You looked good. Both of you.
Actually, I’m here to give you something. It’s in my car. How about the three of us take a walk to it? It’s parked just a ways down the road. I couldn’t get it past your gate.
Elliott, if we’re gonna go that way, you’re gonna need a bigger knife.
Keep stacking. It’ll fit.
Just... yep. There you go.
Get that wouldja, Elliott? Let’s not lose any under the furniture.
Alright. That is nine million, seven hundred and twenty thousand dollars.
I earned it. And you’re going to give it to my children.

On my son’s eighteenth birthday, which is ten months and two days from today, you will give him this money in the form of an irrevocable trust. You’ll tell him it’s his to do with as he sees fit... but with the hope he’ll use it for his college education and for the education of his sister Holly. That, and the general welfare and betterment of his family.

I can’t. My wife, my son, they hate me. They won’t take my money. And even if they did, the federal government wouldn’t let them. But two rich benefactors such as yourselves... two wonderful people who are known for their charitable endeavors, who think nothing of -- for instance -- writing a $28 million dollar check to help victims of methamphetamine abuse... I gotta think your money would be very welcome. Like rain to the desert.
It certainly would. My children are blameless victims of their “monstrous” father -- whom you used to know. Call it a beau geste, call it liberal guilt. Call it what you want, but do it.
And do not spend one dime of your money. If any taxes or lawyer’s fees are owed, it comes out of this right here, you understand? They receive my money. Never yours.
Well... I guess we shake on it, and then I leave. Big day tomorrow. I’ve gotta get ready for it.
Now, I CAN trust you to do this thing? Not just call the police once I’m gone..?
Whoop. Stop, stop. Don’t move. You don’t want them thinking you’re trying to get away.

Just this afternoon, I had an extra two hundred thousand I would’ve dearly loved to leave atop this table. Instead, I gave it to the two best hit men west of the Mississippi. And whatever happens to me tomorrow, they’ll still be out there, keeping tabs. If... for any reason... my children don’t get this money I’ve left you, then a kind of a... a countdown begins. And then, maybe a day later, maybe a week, a year, who knows? You’ll be walking down the street in Santa Fe or Manhattan or Prague, wherever. Talking about your stock price, not a worry in the world. And you’ll hear the scrape of a footstep behind you. And before you can even turn...
Pop. Pop. Darkness.
Cheer up, Beautiful People -- here’s where you get to make it right.
How you feel now?
What’s this I hear about blue meth still being out there..?
Have you heard that? Is it still being sold? By who?
Jesse..?
It’s my birthday.
Before you say or do anything, just hear me out.
No one knows I’m here. Nobody. Just listen to me for two minutes, and then I’ll leave.
Please -- two minutes of your time. You’re running low on methylamine, aren’t you?

Don’t answer -- you don’t have to. I can do the math. You’ve been at it long enough that you must be running low. I’ve got a new method. It doesn’t require methylamine, it doesn’t require pseudo. It requires no Schedule 1 precursors whatsoever. It’s cheap and it’s easy -- and it will keep you in business. And Todd, I can teach it to you.
Ten in the morning every Tuesday, this is where you and I met. You’re very... schedule-oriented, I guess. Look, I just --
I need the money. I’ve spent most of mine staying one step ahead of the police. I don’t have long, and I-I simply... I don’t have long.
Nothing less than a million. And believe me, for this? That’s giving it away.
I can come by tonight, talk to him. I think he’ll get it. He’s still got that place..?
Guys, this is a win-win.
Five minutes.
Didn’t have to.
Yeah. But I feel good.
It’s over, and I needed a proper goodbye. Not our last phone call.
They’ll be coming to me.
They’re not coming back. Not after tonight.
He did. And I don’t have any to give you. I spent the last of it getting here. All I have for you is this.

Once I leave, call the DEA. Tell them I was here, that I forced my way in. Tell them... I wanted bacon and eggs on my birthday. And to see my daughter. And that I gave you that ticket. The numbers are GPS coordinates.
A burial site. That’s where they’ll find Hank and Steve Gomez.

It’s where I buried our money. The men who stole it, the men who have it now, they murdered Hank and Steve. They put them in that hole. Trade that for a deal with the prosecutor. Get yourself out of this.
Skyler, all these things I did... you need to understand why I did them.
-- I did it for me.
I liked it. I was good at it, I was really... I was alive.
Before I go, may I see her? Please.
Couldn’t tell you.
Where to?

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: “Give you a spin?” For Chrissake, I’m not wearing a wire.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: My wallet and keys..?

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Yeah.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Yeah.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Hello to you too, Jack.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: We gonna talk business..?

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Did Todd tell you what I’m offering?

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: You’re running out of methylamine. What happens then?

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Todd, explain things to your uncle, please. Explain to him the benefit of what I’m offering.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Jack --

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: You OWE ME, Jack!

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: For everything! Everything I built! For Jesse Pinkman! You swore you’d kill him -- and instead you partner up, you PARTNER with him?!

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: He’s alive, isn’t he?! He’s cooking for you! What, you’re gonna LIE? You’re gonna deny it?!

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Do it. You want this. Do it.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: I want this.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Hello.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Yeah, it’s done. He’s gone. They’re all gone.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: It’s Walt. How you feeling? Kinda under the weather? Like you’ve got the flu..? That’s the ricin I gave you. I hid it in that stevia crap you’re always putting in your tea.

lines.scene: EXT. JACK’S COMPOUND - MAIN GATE - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Goodbye, Lydia.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Hi.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Nice to meet you.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah, well, you know...

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Honestly, what I do would bore you senseless. Giant space lasers? Now that sounds cool. I’ll have to bring it up at our next staff meeting.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Alright. It’s a deal.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Sure.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Alright.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Ah, the dining “area.” Right.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Pool is nice. Backyard could be a little bigger.
How many bedrooms?
Only three bedrooms? I think we’re gonna need at least five, dontcha think?

No-no-no-no-no. We’ll have three kids total, eventually. You know, but well need a spare room for a study so that I can work at home... and you can write... Yeah, nah. TI don’t think this is gonna be enough.
Very funny. I just think we need to set our sights high is all. At least higher’n here.
Well, then, let’s stretch our price range. Truly. I mean why... why buy a starter house when we’ll have to move out of in a year or two.
I’m serious. C’mon... why be cautious? We’ve got nowhere to go but up.
Yeah.
Yeah. I see you.
And then what? I’m gonna need some... some kind of assurance.
You said no half measures.
Not yet.
Let’s see how this goes first.
Excuse me?
Not that I know of, no.
I’m quite well, thank you.
My partner was about to get himself shot. I intervened.
That’s right. He couldn’t. He was angry because those two dealers of yours had just murdered an eleven year-old boy.
Maybe. Then again, maybe he thought it was you who gave the order.
I would never ask you that.
I wouldn’t know.
A couple of time zones away, at least. Beyond that, I’d only be guessing.
He has enough money to last forever, and he knows to keep moving. You’ll never find him.
He’s out of the picture. I saved his life -- I owed him that. But now he and I are done. Which is exactly what you wanted, isn’t it?

You’ve always struck me as a very pragmatic man. So if I may, I would like to review options with you. Of which, it seems to me, you have two. Option A -- you kill me right here and now. Apparently I have made that very easy for you. You can kill me, no witnesses, and then spend the next few weeks or months tracking down Jesse Pinkman and you kill him, too. A pointless exercise it seems to me, but that is Option A.
I continue cooking. You and I both forget about Pinkman. We forget this ever happened.
We consider this a lone hiccup in an otherwise long and fruitful business arrangement. I prefer Option B.
I could get right on that.
Yeah.
Really?
It’s good to see you.
By all means, Gale. Let’s cook.
That’s two. Alright, let’s close it up.
Alright, bring it down. Ready? Okay, we’re good.
You can take your mask off now.
It’s new. We had some, a uh... ... We had a little drama with the person you replaced.
Nah, nah... it’ll fine. Things’ll continue to smooth out and... yeah. It’ll be fine.
-- No. I’m not.
-- Gale, you’re great. Seriously.
Okay.
What’s up?
No, it’s pretty straightforward. I’ll show you when we get there.
You’re wasting your time -- I’m buying the car wash. End of story.

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: ... Alright, alright, alright already. We’re-we’re good.

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: -- I said “maybe.” Maybe bugged --

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: How you holding up?

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: I got my old job back. At least, until they kill me, and Gale takes over.

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: He’s their boy.

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Well, he asks a lot of questions about the cooking process. I try to be as vague as possible, but I’ve got that guy Victor watching me, listening to every word I say...

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Y’know, it may be that the only thing saving me is Gale’s fastidiousness. Once he feels confident that he knows my entire method...

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: You know what we do.

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Never the DEA.

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: The cook can’t stop. That’s the one thing I’m certain of -- production cannot stop. Gus can’t afford to. So, if I’m the only chemist that he’s got... then I’ve got leverage. And leverage keeps me alive. It keeps you alive, too. I think I can see to that. If I’m the only chemist that he’s got.

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: I’ll do it. I’m gonna need your help. I mean, they’re watching me day and night. They never leave me alone with Gale, not for a moment. Hell, I don’t even know where the man lives. He’s not in the phone book, I can’t find him on the Internet. I can’t do it in the lab. Victor’s always there. But if I could just... shake Victor, for even an hour one night, I think then that.... I may be able to... ... Make it look like an accident.

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: I’m all ears. But when it comes down to you and me versus him? I’m sorry. I’m truly sorry, but it’s gonna be him.

lines.scene: INT. GALACTIC LASER TAG - DAY - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: And you are the only edge that I’ve got, as long as they don’t know that you’re in town. But I need you to track him. Get me his address. And I’ll do the rest. Look, I-I saved your life, Jesse. Are you gonna save mine?
Please tell me you found him.
Yeah. Sixty-three fifty-three Juan Tabo, number six. Got it.
He’s home?
Anyone watching the place?
Tonight. Once it gets dark.
I’ll, uh... I’ll follow you.
Please don’t do this. Mike..? You don’t have to do this.
I-I’ll cook, I’ll cook for free! And there won’t be any more trouble! I promise you. If I could just talk to Gus, I know I can make him understand! Please! If I can talk to Gus, I can convince him...
Just let me, please. Please?! Please let me talk to him!!
I’ll give you Jesse Pinkman! --

Okay? Like you said, he’s the problem! He’s ALWAYS been the problem! Without him -- we would -- And he’s-he’s in TOWN, alright?! He’s-he’s not in Virginia or wherever the hell you’re looking for him -- he’s right here in Albuquerque! And I can take you to him! I’ll take you RIGHT TO him! Huh? What do you say..?
I don’t... He moves, he moves around. But if you let me call him. No, no... please. I just, my phone, it’s just my phone. I’ll call him and have him meet me. Alright? Okay? Okay?
No -- I didn’t do it. I can’t now. It’s gonna have to be you.
Listen to me. You’re closer than we are -- you’ll have about a twenty minute lead.
They’ve got me at the laundry and they’re gonna kill me. Jesse, do it now! Do it fast. Do it, Jesse. Do it!
You might wanna hold off.
Because your boss is gonna need me. Sixty-three fifty-three Juan Tabo, apartment six.
Yeah.
It’s a stupid present...
What was I thinking? The invitation said “no gifts.”
I’m not complaining.

lines.scene: INT. ELLIOTT’S MANSION - ENTRANCE HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: You look nice, honey.

lines.scene: INT. ELLIOTT’S MANSION - ENTRANCE HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Wouldn’t miss it for the world. Happy birthday, Elliott.

lines.scene: INT. ELLIOTT’S MANSION - ENTRANCE HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Good to see you, Gretchen.

lines.scene: INT. ELLIOTT’S MANSION - ENTRANCE HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: That’s so great. Oh, and congratulations on the Nobel Prize. The research you’ve been doing... it’s phenomenal.

lines.scene: INT. ELLIOTT’S MANSION - ENTRANCE HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Definitely.

lines.scene: INT. ELLIOTT’S MANSION - ENTRANCE HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Oh my God. I count six Nobel laureates in this room.
No, thank you.
Hey, Farley. Long time no see. 12.
They generate purer and more complete patterns than X-ray beams. Data collection takes a fraction of the time.
Back when Elliott and I were in grad school, we came up with the name. Schwartz -- black. Walter White. Black and white make gray... Gray Matter Technologies.
Actually, no. I ended up going into education. 13.

lines.scene: INT. ELLIOTT’S MANSION - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: For the man who has everything.
At least I didn’t destroy the microwave with my experiments.
All you had to do was mention the Bunsen burner and he’d go off on a rant. “He didn’t actually invent it, he just improved it.” Easy way to kill fifteen minutes. 16.
Me, too.
We should get together more often. Skyler would love to have you and Gretchen over for dinner sometime.
You want me to work for Gray Matter?
Yeah, as a high school teacher. Can’t even remember the last time I set foot in a real lab. I’ve been out of the loop for twenty years.
I wouldn’t even know where to begin. You have no idea... I spend my day drawing atoms on a chalkboard. Making kids memorize the periodic table.
Elliott... this is... this is very appealing. But you should know... I’ve got some... personal issues.
It’s complicated.
You gotta jiggle it.
What the fuck did you say to Elliott?
-- You told him about the cancer, didn’t you?
How about “fine”?
Oh, please.
He offered me a job!
That’s what you wanted, right?
Well, what did you think he was gonna do? You tell the man I’m dying --
-- Whatever. Whatever, alright?! He’s a multi-millionaire! What’s he gonna say, “Sorry, too bad, you’re on your own?”
-- Oh yes, he would. Because when I turned down the job, he offered to simply pay for the treatment.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - DINING ROOM - MORNING
lines.dialogue: Need a ride? WALTER, JR. I’m taking the bus.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: I’m the one who’s sick --

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: Fine.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: Am I allowed to answer?

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: SHUT UP! SHUT THE FUCK UP!

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: I’ve got the Talking Pillow now.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: I’ve listened to everything you had to say. And I appreciate how much thought you’ve put into my situation. But don’t you think I’ve gone through all this in my head a thousand times and weighed all my options? 40.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: You think taking a handout from Elliott is the answer. But nothing is ever “no strings attached.” I’ll never be able to pay him back. And after I die, you’re gonna be indebted to him forever. Do you really want that hanging over you?

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: Well, I do. And I would prefer to die holding my head up high, rather than eating shit.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: -- Why? That’s what this is all about, isn’t it? You’re trying to delay the inevitable by putting me through some experimental treatment that may not even work. It doesn’t come with a guarantee. I could go through hell and still end up dead.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: Of course I do. But you have to accept the fact that... it’s not gonna happen. You heard the doctor. Best case scenario, even with the treatment... it’d be a miracle if I made it to her third birthday. 41.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: What good is another year of survival if I’m spending that time undergoing chemo and radiation, too sick to work or have sex or even enjoy a meal? I don’t want to take twenty pills a day. And -- no offense, Hank -- I don’t want to lose my hair. And I don’t want to feel like shit all the time.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING
lines.dialogue: I know that -- and that’s the worst part. You and Walter, Jr. are gonna be taking care of me when I can’t function anymore. You’re gonna be sticking me with IV’s and emptying my bedpan and cleaning up my puke. When I die, that is what you’re gonna remember about me. And I’m sorry, but I don’t wanna be remembered that way. I didn’t get a choice about getting cancer. This is the only choice I get to make.
Okay.
I’ll do the treatment.
It’s gonna be okay.
Hello? INTERCUT WITH: 44.
Hi. How are you?
I’m okay. Really.

Absolutely not. And I appreciate the offer. But it turns out my insurance came through after all. The HMO is gonna cover a majority of the treatment. Guess the teachers union is good for something, huh?
But thank you anyway. It was very kind of you and Elliott.
Sure. And thanks for calling.
Wanna cook? CUT TO BLACK.
Huh.
Same time.
Hey.
Eat it.
All set? Alright, see you at home.
Chemistry is the study of what?

Chemicals. No. Change. Chemistry is the study of change. Think about it. Electrons change their orbits, molecules change their bonds. Elements combine and change into compounds. That’s all of life, right? The constant... The cycle. Solution, dissolution, over and over.
Growth, decay. Transformation. It’s fascinating, really.
Chad, keep your hands to yourself please. Is there something wrong with your own table?
Alright, ionic bonds. Chapter six.

lines.scene: INT. HIGH SCHOOL - FACULTY WORKROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Hey, Margaret.

lines.scene: INT. HIGH SCHOOL - FACULTY WORKROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Happy Birthday.

lines.scene: INT. HIGH SCHOOL - FACULTY WORKROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: My lips are sealed.

lines.scene: INT. HIGH SCHOOL - FACULTY WORKROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Those things’ll kill you, you know.
-- Eight, nine, ten, and ten makes twenty. Thank you. Come again.
Amir, no. We talked about this. Inside only. And only till six.
Oh, shit. 11.
No. Thank you. Let’s, please, let’s change the subject.
Hank? How much money is that?
That’s got to be unusual, right? That kind of cash? 14.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - MASTER BEDROOM/BATHROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Which one’s this?

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - MASTER BEDROOM/BATHROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: How’s it doing?

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - MASTER BEDROOM/BATHROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: What’s up?

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - MASTER BEDROOM/BATHROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Actually, I was thinking about, um. Maybe drive to Caltech.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - MASTER BEDROOM/BATHROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yeah, I’ll mow. JPL’s got an exhibit of Mars rover photographs. Supposed to be, the detail... just really amazing. Really beautiful.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - MASTER BEDROOM/BATHROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I will mow. First thing.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - MASTER BEDROOM/BATHROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I’m just... we gotta be careful of the baby.
Hey. Yeah, sorry. I had it turned off. I was, uh... Yeah, probably about an hour or so.
I’m at Caltech. I ran into an old professor, we got to talking. I should be home in about an hour. Okay.
I’ve had it before. Low blood sugar. Stood up too fast. 19.
Guess I should’ve had breakfast this morning.
Oncologist...

lines.scene: INT. DR. BELKNAP’S OFFICE/EXAM AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah. DR. BELKNAP Did you..? You understood what I’ve said to you?

lines.scene: INT. DR. BELKNAP’S OFFICE/EXAM AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah. Multiple myeloma. Stage 3. Best-case scenario, with chemo, I’ll live another two years. It’s just, you’ve got mustard on your... you’ve got mustard there.
You know. Same. 22.
No, just. Today.
Uh. We needed printer paper.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: Hey. Your Mom wants you to turn it down. WALTER, JR. Shit, come--on. This is--the best-- Wait, wait... 23.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: DVD? WALTER, JR. Uncle Hank--gave--it to me.

lines.scene: INT. WHITE HOUSE - SPARE BEDROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Two years. 24.
Hank? Hey, it’s Walt. I didn’t wake you, did I? Good. Listen, I’ve been thinking. Could I take you up on your offer? The ride-along? CUT TO:
Yeah.
That’s a meth lab. 25.
Phosgene gas, I think.
Hank? Do you think I might get to go inside? See the lab?
God. Dupree..?
Nothing.
It’s me. I’m alone.
You’re still in our filing system. Your aunt owns this place, right?
Nobody’s looking for you.
